Public Methods Manual
:::

BNR mortality statistics describe deaths that meet the Registry's practical cardiovascular mortality classification. The dashboard reports **numbers of deaths**, **percentage distributions** and annual **mortality rates** using two related definitions: **Primary** and **Inclusive**.

## At a glance

| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| **Question answered** | How many deaths meet the BNR cardiovascular mortality classification, and how are those deaths distributed across broad groups? |
| **Source** | Death-certificate information held by the Registration Department of the Supreme Court of Barbados and converted to electronic records by the BNR |
| **Primary definition** | Clear + Likely BNR cardiovascular mortality classifications |
| **Inclusive definition** | Clear + Likely + Possible BNR cardiovascular mortality classifications |
| **Reported as** | Counts, percentage distributions, and annual rates per 100,000 population |
| **Current dashboard period** | Published calendar periods from 2010 onwards, according to the current approved release |

[Open the CVD mortality dashboard](../../surveillance/cvd/metrics/mortality/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## What does the dashboard show?

The dashboard has three main views.

**Number of deaths** shows how many deaths meet the selected BNR mortality definition during a month, quarter or year.

**Distribution of deaths** shows how the published deaths are divided between categories such as Heart and Stroke, women and men, or the broad age groups used for annual reporting.

**Mortality rates** show the number of deaths per 100,000 residents, allowing fairer comparison across periods and population groups of different sizes.

These three views answer different questions. A count describes how many deaths were classified. A percentage describes how those classified deaths were divided between categories. A rate describes the number of deaths relative to the population, allowing fair comparison between population groups or periods of different sizes.

## Annual mortality rates

The mortality-rate view reports the number of classified deaths per 100,000 Barbados population for each complete calendar year. It is available for All CVD, Heart and Stroke; both sexes, women and men; and the Primary and Inclusive definitions.

Two forms are published:

- **Crude rate:** classified deaths divided by the matching annual population.
- **Age-standardised rate (ASR):** age-specific rates combined using the fixed WHO World Standard Population (2000-2025), so comparisons over time or between sex groups are less affected by differences in age structure.

Population denominators use the approved UN World Population Prospects 2024 Barbados series. Crude-rate intervals use the exact Poisson (Garwood) method and ASR intervals use the Fay-Feuer gamma method. The intervals describe statistical variation inherent in the published rates. They do not quantify uncertainty from death classification or from changes in death-certificate completeness over time.

Where an annual death count is protected for confidentiality (for counts 5 or lower), its matching rate and CI are also unavailable. 

## Primary and Inclusive definitions

The mortality classifier records different levels of evidence. The dashboard uses two nested definitions.

| Dashboard definition | What it includes | How to interpret it |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary** | Clear + Likely | The main BNR reporting definition |
| **Inclusive** | Clear + Likely + Possible | A broader definition that includes deaths where cardiovascular attribution is plausible but more uncertain |

The Inclusive definition contains the Primary definition. They are **alternative ways of describing the same mortality burden and must not be added together**.

For example, if 80 deaths meet the Primary definition and another 12 deaths are classified as Possible, the Inclusive count is 92. It is not 172.

For more detail, see [How CVD deaths are classified](../interpretation/classifying-cvd-deaths.qmd).

## Time periods and available breakdowns

The dashboard deliberately uses different levels of detail at different time scales.

| Time period | Published breakdowns |
|---|---|
| **Monthly** | All CVD, both sexes and all ages only |
| **Quarterly** | All CVD, Heart and Stroke; both sexes, women and men |
| **Annual** | All CVD, Heart and Stroke; both sexes, women and men; broad age groups for All CVD where available |

The restricted monthly view reduces unnecessary disclosure risk. More detailed monthly breakdowns are not produced simply because the data exist privately.

## Monthly historical context

Monthly counts are shown against a fixed 2015&mdash;2019 historical reference.

For each calendar month, the dashboard shows:

- the lowest monthly count seen during 2015&mdash;2019;
- the highest monthly count seen during 2015&mdash;2019; and
- the average count for that calendar month during the same five-year period.

## Quarterly and annual comparisons

Instead of a fixed 2015&mdash;2019 historical reference, quarterly and annual count views can be compared against a *rolling average* from the previous five comparable years. So, an annual count for 2025 can be compared against the average of 5 values from 2020 to 2024. A quarterly count for the 1st quarter of 2025 can be compared against the average of 5 1st-quarter counts between 2020 and 2024.     

## Percentage distributions

Percentage distributions describe the **mix of classified CVD deaths**. They do not describe an individual's risk of dying and they are not population mortality rates.

For example, a chart showing 30% Heart and 70% Stroke means that, among the published CVD deaths in that definition and period, 30% were classified as Heart and 70% as Stroke.

See [Counts, percentages and rates](../interpretation/counts-percentages-rates.qmd) for the distinction between these forms of statistic.

## Protected values

BNR applies disclosure control before mortality data are published. Any period containing a count of 5 or smaller will be suppressed, and is shown using an asterisk (**\***). See more on [protecting confidentiality](../interpretation/confidentiality.qmd).

## How the BNR death classification system differs from official cause-of-death statistics

The BNR method is a practical surveillance classification used while a formally assigned national **underlying cause of death** is not available to BNR for this purpose.

It uses death-certificate wording and structure to assign approximate cardiovascular mortality classifications. It is **not full ICD-10 underlying-cause coding** and does not reproduce an official automated cause-of-death coding system.

BNR mortality counts should therefore not be assumed to be directly equivalent to official national or international mortality series that use formal ICD-10 underlying-cause-of-death rules.

## Release date and latest data period

The date on which a mortality release is published may be later than the latest death period included in that release. The dashboard shows these separately. This reporting lag may reduce over time, but the release date should never be interpreted as the date of the latest underlying observation.

## Mortality is not case fatality

Mortality counts describe deaths classified through the mortality surveillance source. [Case fatality](case-fatality.qmd) describes the proportion of eligible hospital CVD events ending in death under the case-fatality definition. They answer different questions and use different analytical denominators.

## What to remember

- *Primary* is the main BNR mortality definition; *Inclusive* is a broader sensitivity definition.
- *Primary* and *Inclusive* are alternatives and must not be added together.
- Monthly reporting is intentionally restricted to All CVD, both sexes and all ages.
- BNR mortality classifications are not identical to formal ICD-10 underlying-cause-of-death statistics.
